THEOREM 1: A Comparison Test for Improper Integrals

Let \(f\) and \(g\) be positive integrable functions and \(0\leq f(x)\leq g(x)\) for all \( x\in [a,\infty)\). By the monotone property of the integral \[0\leq \displaystyle\int_a^\infty g(x)dx \leq \int_a^\infty g(x)dx\]

  1. If \(\displaystyle\int_a^\infty g(x)dx\) converges, then \(\displaystyle\int_a^\infty f(x)dx\) converges.
  2. On the other hand, if \(\displaystyle\int_a^\infty f(x)dx\) diverges, then \(\displaystyle\int_a^\infty g(x)dx\) also diverges.
  3. The same results hold for the other types of improper integrals.

THEOREM 2: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), then the function \(F\) defined by \[F(x)=\int_a^xf(t)dt\] is differentiable on \((a,b)\) and its derivative is given by \(F'(x)=f(x)\). i.e \(\displaystyle\int_a^xf(t)dt\) is an antiderivative for \(f(x)\) on \((a,b)\). STACK inputs writting
